selections.description: Cloud iMessage space routing, outbound content/actions, attachments and advanced builder delivery, with original cloud-provider tests.
acceptance: Original space, reactions, unsend and read-action scenarios map to real native binary requests, preserving shared/dedicated routing, explicit phone identity, canonical phone/space checks and parent GUID plus part index.

Preserve text/link/binary/group sends, ordered variadic sends/replies, typing cleanup and authoritative getMessage without cache-first resolution. Native failures propagate with actionable typed errors; no mock-only success path.

Evaluate every selected original Markdown, stream-text, app-card, poll, membership, background, contact and advanced-action scenario. Adopt supported Web behavior with executable tests or report the exact provider/macOS/dependency/pinned-wire-contract blocker. Native RPC exposure alone is not builder or event parity.

Web attachments use raw Uint8Array/Blob/URL, preserve multipart identities and use existing app-owned download/upload cancellation and cleanup. Do not recreate filesystem inputs, ffmpeg/image subprocesses or Buffer wrappers.

Add source-linked upstream-derived regressions and docs/ports receipts containing immutable source/test URLs, original SHA-256 hashes, target tests, explicit adaptations and unimplemented scenarios. Preserve all existing tests and original manifest pins; no test-count mirroring, skipped placeholders or weakened assertions.
Supported APIs remain reachable from existing public indexes and standalone imessage/umbrella packages and pass packed workerd execution without Node globals or compatibility flags.

instructions.goal: Implement and track cloud-provider send/action behavior using the existing Web facade and exact pinned wire contract, including meaningful advanced capabilities where supportable.
adaptation: Read docs/UPSTREAM-COMPATIBILITY.md and docs/COMPATIBILITY-PLAN.md. The baseline is an acknowledged partial port, not a parity certificate; original upstream tests are semantic evidence, not a requirement to reproduce private Node mocks.

Reuse SpectrumLines, native clients, materialization, builder resolution and app lifetime; do not introduce a second credential inventory or provider framework. Lifecycle/inbound tests are owned by the following policy; their source remains dependency context here.

Use existing public indexes for exports. Manifests, scripts and gates are protected; any necessary new dependency/package/export-map entry needs an architecture decision in docs/ports and separately approved scope, never verification weakening.
Do real runtime/test work for supported cases. An impossible capability requires a concrete blocked decision, not fabricated behavior or a blanket documentation-only success.
nonGoals: Other providers, local Apple database/macOS integrations, wholesale framework transplantation or upstream Node transport installation.
Cache-first getMessage, Node/Bun polyfills, nodejs_compat, copied generated assets or unsupported invented protobuf/wire operations.

preserve: Update current usage and compatibility documentation when behavior changes, while retaining original test attribution, license notices and historical baseline coverage. New support is not evidence that old tests were rebased.
Preserve existing SDK work and public names/signatures; api, webhooks, imessage and umbrella remain independently usable. Use standard Web APIs and existing binary gRPC-Web/management contracts only.

One SpectrumLines inventory and app lifetime; authoritative uncached getMessage; canonical phone/space guards; multipart identities; raw Uint8Array; awaited authenticated webhook callbacks; bounded lazy iterators with propagated errors and cancellation.

Never delete, skip, relax or replace meaningful existing tests to pass. Do not bypass protected boundary/provenance/audit checks through fixtures or production special cases. Keep original tests/upstream-manifest.json pins unchanged; future partial-port links/hashes and executable test mappings go in docs/ports.
Package manifests, lockfiles, scripts, CI and policy/check/source-audit runners must not change. New dependency/package/export decisions require human approval outside this policy.
